subject: KiteChain reserved-capacity: traffic clarifications & capacity playbook
body:
From: Jesse Park <jesse@kitechain.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@kitechain.com
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reserved capacity sizing inputs (sample attached)

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. We got good alignment internally on wanting a reserved GPU pool for inference (low-latency API calls for our fraud-detection product). Before we commit, legal/procurement want a short, concrete sizing checklist so they can map to our budget and cloud approvals. I attached a CSV with a 2-week token/req sample exported from our telemetry.

Can you confirm the minimum questions you need answered to produce a preliminary reserved capacity plan and a sample monthly cost estimate? Our initial requirements: p99 latency target 120ms, end user facing API (US region), peak concurrent sessions ~220, average request prompt+response tokens ~1,200, percent of streaming responses ~15%.

Best,
Jesse

---

On Tue, 14 Jul 2026 at 10:03 AM kimberly_park@redwood.ai wrote:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Jesse Park <jesse@kitechain.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity sizing inputs (sample attached)

Hi Jesse — appreciate the CSV. Quick read-through looks useful. To produce a robust reserved-capacity playbook (and a conservative cost estimate) we typically need the following minimal clarifications — this will let us size GPU SKUs, KV-cache sizing, and burst/overtime buffers: 

- Traffic shape: steady baseline RPS vs peak RPS, and the duration of peak windows (minutes/hours). If you have 95th/99th percentile windows, include those.
- Session model: are calls independent stateless API calls, or do you maintain long-lived sessions with KV cache warmed (session lengths / avg messages per session)?
- Prompt/response distribution: percent of short (<256 tokens), medium (256–1024), long (>1024) responses; you gave avg 1,200 but distribution matters for latency & memory.
- Streaming vs non-streaming ratio (you mentioned ~15%), and whether streaming calls typically have similar token counts or longer tails.
- SLOs per route: any routes stricter than p99 120ms (e.g., search index lookup route).
- Acceptable fallback behavior: if reserved pool is saturated, should we failover to hosted pool (higher cost, lower latency SLA) or queue?
- Security/compliance constraints: do you require VPC-only private deployment or is Hosted/Dedicated hybrid acceptable?

If you can answer the bullets above and share a 48–72 hour high-resolution token-by-second sample (CSV), Marissa can run the sizing simulator and I can produce a playbook that includes recommended GPU SKU mix, KV cache sizing, expected token-unit cost, and a recommended buffer (we usually size with 25% burst headroom).

I attached a short template (redwood_prelim_sizing.pdf) showing the outputs you'll get.

Thanks — Kim

---

On Wed, 15 Jul 2026 at 08:17 AM Jesse Park <jesse@kitechain.com> wrote:
From: Jesse Park <jesse@kitechain.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@kitechain.com
Date: Wed, 15 Jul 2026 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity sizing inputs (sample attached)

Kimberly — thanks for the checklist. Answers below and I attached a cropped high-res 72h sample as requested.

- Traffic shape: baseline ~30 RPS, sustained peak ~210 RPS for 2–4 hour windows during business hours (US PST), with microbursts up to 320 RPS lasting 2–5 minutes (marketing-driven spikes).
- Session model: mostly stateless calls (80%), but we have a personalization path (~20%) that uses short-lived session affinities with warm KV state (avg 6 messages/session).
- Prompt/response distribution: short 10%, medium 55%, long 35% (longs commonly for investigative queries).
- Streaming: 15% of total; streaming calls average 1,800 tokens (longer tail).
- SLOs: p99 120ms for priority route A (payment fraud check), p95 200ms for other routes.
- Fallback: prefer automatic failover to Redwood hosted pool during sustained saturation (we accept higher cost for continuity), but we'd like rate-limited queuing for short microbursts.
- Security: Dedicated (VPC) required for production, but proof-of-concept pilot can use Hybrid.

I'll loop procurement if you need formal wording for the PO.

Regards,
Jesse

---

On Fri, 16 Jul 2026 at 11:03 AM kimberly_park@redwood.ai wrote:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Jesse Park <jesse@kitechain.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, procurement@kitechain.com
Date: Fri, 16 Jul 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity sizing inputs (sample attached)

Thanks Jesse — that is exactly the level of detail we need. Next steps and deliverables from Redwood: 

1) We will run the 72h high-res sample through our sizing simulator (Marissa will lead). Deliverable: a 2-page capacity playbook that includes GPU SKU mix (preferred + backup), KV cache RAM targets, expected token-unit op cost, and recommended 25% headroom. (ETA 48 hours).

2) We will produce two cost scenarios: (A) conservative (lower-cost SKUs + slightly higher queueing tolerance), (B) premium (stronger p99 headroom, more hot capacity).

3) We will draft a short failure-mode section that specifies automatic failover routing to Redwood hosted pool and short-queue behavior for microbursts (matches your ask).

4) Action items for KiteChain: confirm whether the personalization path requires session persistence across multiple requests from the same end user device (i.e., sticky sessions), and share any secret-scoped KV schema sizes if available.

Attachments: redwood_prelim_sizing.pdf (template), KiteChain_MAPlist.xlsx (we added a simple mapping worksheet for your team to fill).

I'll have Marissa send the preliminary playbook and a slide summarizing the cost scenarios to your HubSpot deal link. If procurement wants an SOW stub to include pricing bands, we can provide an initial draft next week.

Kim
Customer Success & Pre-Sales, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0132

--
Attachment stubs: kitechain_sample_traffic.csv (72h high-res sample), kitechain_72h_highres_trim.csv (cropped sample attached by Jesse), redwood_prelim_sizing.pdf, KiteChain_MAPlist.xlsx
